chunks: A number of our companions, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Abi Abdullah, raised it from Abu Abdullah (peace be upon him) who said:

Rasool-Allah (peace be upon him and his family) said: 'Two commanders, yet they are not two commanders in status: It is not for the one who follows a coffin to return until he is permitted, and a man who performs Hajj with a woman, so it is not for him to depart (abandon her) until she has fulfilled her rituals.'
ai.seo_question: What are the rules for leaving a funeral procession and accompanying a woman during Hajj?
ai.summary: This hadith from al-Kafi highlights the principle of *ittiba'* (following) in both social and ritual contexts, emphasizing the duty of companionship until the completion of the respective obligations. Scholarly tradition interprets the 'two commanders' as distinct legal precedents: one governing the etiquette of funeral rites (*janazah*) and the other regulating the logistics of Hajj when a husband accompanies his wife, ensuring she is not left alone during her pilgrimage rituals.
